title: Admissible Determination: Legitimate Selectivity, Observation, and Time in Structura Reditus
object_of_study: The adequacy of selective representations for independently specified targets, with time as the principal application.
main_question: When can a representation omit source distinctions without losing an independently specified answer, and what evidence repairs a target-changing loss?
secondary_questions: When does model-relative determination cover the intended application?
Which temporal burdens require distinct calibration, latency, clock, or provenance evidence?

claim_layers.claim: Exact target recovery through an admitted representation is equivalent to constancy on its observational fibers; a target may remain identifiable without complete-state recovery.
A coverage condition separates model-relative determination from application adequacy; finite-menu repair separates target-changing alternatives with distinguishing evidence.
Time is the principal application: order, interval, rate, epoch, calibration, latency, present-state inference, proper time, provenance, and civil labels have distinct preservation burdens.

Version 1.1.0 declares a retrospective external-evidence freeze with source cutoff September 20 2026, retaining the RFC timestamp fixture and bounded IERS, BIPM, distributed-time, optical-clock, archival, and IANA witnesses. No new physical experiment, prospective deployment validation, canonical return, or weld is claimed.

Library classification: diagnostic primary with domain-translation secondary, reflecting the paper's conditional adequacy tests and application interfaces. These retrieval labels are not source-native claims of new authority.
